deep.reconstruction:
Context. The heading reads 'Bemerkungen zu der allgemeinen Formel' (remarks on the general formula). The text addresses a 'Sie', so these are comments to a correspondent. The following page uses Riemann's minimal-surface variables η, η', X, X'. This strongly suggests (my inference) remarks on a draft write-up of Riemann's minimal-surface theory. The obvious candidate is K. Hattendorff, who edited 'Ueber die Fläche vom kleinsten Inhalt bei gegebener Begrenzung' (published 1867). The page sets up sign and orientation conventions for the area integral and its variation.

(1) Normal of a graph. The surface is written as x = x(y,z). Its tangent plane is dx − x_y dy − x_z dz = 0. The same plane in normal-angle form is cos r dx + sin r cos θ dy + sin r sin θ dz = 0. Here r is the angle of the 'positive normal' with the +x axis and θ is its azimuth in the (y,z) plane. Comparing coefficients and normalising gives:
- cos r = ±1/√(1+x_y²+x_z²),
- sin r cos θ = ∓x_y/√(…),
- sin r sin θ = ∓x_z/√(…) (the third is implicit; my completion).
The upper signs hold when the positive normal makes an acute angle with the +x axis, the lower signs otherwise. First remark: the two sides of the surface must be distinguished as positive and negative.

(2) Area, option A. Take dy dz as the area of the projection of the surface element on the (y,z) plane, with dy, dz always positive (sides of a rectangle). Then
- area = ∬ √(1+x_y²+x_z²) dy dz = ∬ (±1/cos r) dy dz.
The sign must be chosen pointwise according to the sign of cos r.

(3) Area, option B. Introduce parameters p, q distinguishing the points of the surface. The deleted lines say no pair (p,q) should occur twice and give conditions on the curves (p), (q). Then (y_q z_p − y_p z_q) dp dq, with dp, dq > 0, is the signed area of the projection onto the (y,z) plane of the infinitesimal parallelogram bounded by the curves (q), (q+dq), (p), (p+dp).
- The sign is + or − according as, seen from the +x side, side (p) is brought into coincidence with side (q) by a positive or negative rotation through an acute angle.
- Positive rotation means +y axis towards +z axis.

(4) Consistent orientation. Suppose the parametrisation is coherently oriented. That is, seen from the positive normal, side (p) lies on the same side of side (q) for every infinitesimal parallelogram, say always the 'positive' side. Then the projected orientation seen from +x agrees with the orientation seen from the normal exactly when the normal makes an acute angle with +x (cos r > 0). It is reversed when cos r < 0.
- Hence (y_q z_p − y_p z_q) dp dq has the sign of cos r.
- So dA = (1/cos r)(y_q z_p − y_p z_q) dp dq is always positive. This is the area element, with no case split.
- In modern terms: the x-component of the oriented area vector satisfies n_x dA = ±∂(y,z)/∂(p,q) dp dq, and r_p × r_q (or r_q × r_p) is the positive normal times dA.

(5) Special choice. Choose the curves so that y is constant on one family and z on the other (p ≈ y, q ≈ z locally). Then the element becomes (1/cos r) dy dz. Now dy, dz are no longer always positive: they carry whatever signs make the corresponding dp, dq positive.

(6) Purpose. This last form is recommended for computing the area. It is also recommended for transforming the first variation by partial integration (continued on 13v): one then need not separate the parts of the surface where cos r > 0 and cos r < 0. On the next page, Jacobian integrals ∬ ∂(f,g)/∂(p,q) dp dq are converted to boundary integrals ∫ f g_q dq taken in the positive direction. This only requires that the boundary integrand sin r cos φ δx dz + sin r sin φ δx dy (as transcribed) vary continuously, even where cos r = 0.
errors: No mathematical error. The sign of y_q z_p − y_p z_q is the negative of the usual Jacobian ∂(y,z)/∂(p,q); this is absorbed in Riemann's stated rotation convention ('side (p) rotated into side (q)') and his choice of which side is 'positive'.
Unstated assumption: a coherent orientation of the (p,q) net must exist globally, i.e. the surface is two-sided. This is implicit in 'the two sides must be distinguished'.

The phrase 'links liegen' (lie to the left) seen from larger x, paired with 'negative Seite', is somewhat loosely worded. The logical content (sign of the Jacobian = sign of cos r) is nonetheless correct.

results.what: Normal direction cosines of a graph x = x(y,z): cos r = ±1/√(1+x_y²+x_z²), sin r cos θ = ∓x_y/√(…), with sign tied to a chosen positive side.
results.modern_name: Unit normal of a graph / oriented surface

results.what: Area element as ∬√(1+x_y²+x_z²) dy dz = ∬ dy dz/|cos r|, and in parameters as (1/cos r)·(Jacobian of the (y,z)-projection) dp dq, made sign-free by a coherent orientation.
results.modern_name: Surface area element; projection formula n_x dA = dy∧dz for oriented surfaces
results.usually_credited_to: Lagrange (1760, minimal surfaces); Gauss 1827 (Disquisitiones generales circa superficies curvas)

results.what: Using an oriented parametrisation so that the variational boundary terms from partial integration need no splitting of the surface where cos r changes sign.
results.modern_name: Integration of differential forms over an oriented surface / Stokes-type reduction in the first variation
results.usually_credited_to: Green, Ostrogradsky, Stokes (1828–1854), later formalised by Poincaré and Cartan

deep.surprise_reason: These are careful but standard orientation and sign conventions for the area integral, apparently written as editorial remarks on a draft of Riemann's minimal-surface paper. Historically mildly interesting as evidence of how the posthumous 1867 paper was prepared, but mathematically routine for the period.

checkable.asserts: (cos r, sin r cos θ, sin r sin θ) = ±(1, −x_y, −x_z)/√(1+x_y²+x_z²) is normal to the graph's tangent plane.
For parameters (y,z) the area element of x = x(y,z) is √(1+x_y²+x_z²) dy dz.

checkable.sympy: p,q=symbols('p q'); x,y,z=[Function(n)(p,q) for n in 'xyz']; R=Matrix([x,y,z]); C=R.diff(q).cross(R.diff(p)); simplify(C[0]-(diff(y,q)*diff(z,p)-diff(y,p)*diff(z,q)))==0
checkable.asserts: y_q z_p − y_p z_q is the x-component of r_q × r_p. So with n = (r_q×r_p)/|r_q×r_p|, one has cos r·dA = (y_q z_p − y_p z_q) dp dq and dA = (1/cos r)(y_q z_p − y_p z_q) dp dq > 0.
Next-page identity: the Jacobian f_p g_q − f_q g_p is a divergence, enabling reduction to a boundary integral.

transcription_corrections: Line 1 end: 'wie [?] cos θ = ∓ ...' should read 'sin r cos θ = ∓ (∂x/∂y)/√(...)'; the image shows 'sin r cos θ'.
Line 1: the first sentence ends with 'unterscheiden' followed by a comma/dash, not a full stop.

'Bei dem Ausdruck des Inhalts der Fläche können Sie nun entweder stets ... betrachten, also dy, dz' is duplicated in the transcription. The image has one line ending '...betrachten, also dy, dz' followed by 'dy dz als Inhalt der Projection des Flächenelements auf die (y,z) Ebene'.
'eine positive oder negativen spitzen Winkel {+mit der+} macht' is more likely 'einen positiven oder negativen spitzen Winkel mit ihr macht' (superscript 'mit ihr').
'Für alle unendlich kleinen Flächenelemente' is an interlinear insertion above 'Von der positiven Normalen aus gesehen'.
'zum Zusammenfallen mit der Seite (p) durch eine positive oder negative Drehung' is probably preceded by 'die Seite (q)'. The sense is that side (p) is turned to coincide with side (q).
